title: Ameyn/gdn stp replayssm kernel
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

feat(gdn): STP (T=1) ucache decode kernel
Adds flashinfer/gdn_kernels/gdn_decode_bf16_wy_ucache_stp.py: a
self-contained GDN (gated delta rule) decode kernel for single-token
prediction with a u-cache. Instead of rewriting the [HV, V, K] SSM state
on every decoded token, each step appends the token's update ingredients
(L2-normalized k, delta-rule correction u, log-decay g) to a small
16-slot per-request cache and reads the state WITHOUT writing it; the
state is rewritten only on a periodic flush. This removes the per-step
state write from steady-state decode while keeping outputs equivalent to
the standard per-token state update.

Entry point: gated_delta_rule_stp_ucache_flush. SM90+; K == V == 128.

Inputs (IO dtype = bf16 default, fp16 via GDN_UCACHE_IO_DTYPE; STATE and
RING dtypes default to IO, fp16 selectable via GDN_UCACHE_STATE_DTYPE /
GDN_UCACHE_RING_DTYPE; all GEMM accumulation and gate math in fp32):
```
  q, k                  [B, 1, H, K]       IO
  v                     [B, 1, HV, V]      IO
  a, b                  [B, 1, HV]         IO
  A_log, dt_bias        [HV]               cast + cached to IO
  initial_state_source  [pool, HV, V, K]   STATE  (read-only except flush)
  initial_state_indices [B]                int32
  k_cache               [pool, H,  16, K]  RING
  u_cache               [pool, HV, 16, V]  RING
  g_cache               [pool, HV, 16]     fp32
  hist_len              [B]                int32  (cache fill; committed
                                                   in place every call)
  cache_base            [B]                int32  (must be zeros)
  scale                 float
```
q/k/v/a/b may alternatively be passed prepadded as persistent [B, 4, ...]
buffers (row 0 real, rows 1..3 zero) -- a zero-copy serving fast path
that removes all per-step staging copies.

Outputs: the decoded token's output [B, 1, HV, V] in the IO dtype. Each
verify step also appends exactly one (k, u, g) entry at cache slot
hist_len and commits hist_len += 1 (single fused kernel, CUDA-graph
safe).

Flush: when a request arrives with hist_len == flush_min (default 15,
legal range [1, 15]), the kernel folds the cached window AND the current
token into the state pool -- S <- e^G * S + sum_j w_j u_j k_j^T, one
fp32-accumulated rewrite with a single rounding to the STATE dtype --
and the cache restarts empty (hist_len <- 0). Steady state: 15 read-only
steps + 1 flush per 16 decoded tokens.

Correctness -- 27 STP tests added to the existing ucache suite (its fp32
oracle, dtype arms, and case builder are generalized to T=1 and reused;
no new test file). Run:

  pytest tests/gdn/test_decode_ucache.py -k stp

Coverage: all 5 dtype arms, exhaustive cache depths P in [0, 15],
shuffled non-identity state indices, single-append audits, multistep
fold cycles, a 200-step drift run against a never-resynced fp32
reference (max output error 6.5e-4, flat across 12 flush cycles), and
the prepadded path bitwise-matching the default path.

Benchmark -- extends the existing harness with --kernel stp (default
--kernel mtp behavior unchanged). Run:

`  python benchmarks/bench_gdn_ucache_flush.py --kernel stp --rates 0 100`

B200, bf16, CUDA-graph replay, CUPTI cold-L2 timing, median of 300:
```
     B | verify step (us) | flush step (us)
     8 |            11.8  |           17.8
    16 |            15.4  |           24.7
    32 |            25.3  |           42.4
    64 |            43.2  |           76.1
   128 |            74.4  |          143.1
   256 |           134.9  |          274.8
```

title: fix(kda): force min_blocks_per_mp=1 on SM107 in WY output-only decode
body:
## 📌 Description

The KDA WY output-only decode kernel faults on SM107 (cc 10.7, Rubin) once its grid needs more than
one wave: `Xid 13` → sticky `cudaErrorLaunchFailure`. This is the same CuTe DSL defect as #4957 —
with `min_blocks_per_mp > 1` and no explicit `preferred_smem_carveout`, the DSL auto-derives a
preferred SMEM carveout and applies it at module load — in the kernel that was *derived from* the GDN
WY decode kernel #5227 fixes. That kernel and this one share their PTX/layout helpers verbatim (see
the note at the top of `kda_decode_wy_output_only.py`), including the launch-bound formula:

| | GDN WY decode (fixed in #5227) | KDA WY output-only decode (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| launch bound | `mbp = max(1, min(_needed + 1, 8))` | identical, `:2328` and `:2552` |
| carveout | none | none (`:2385`, `:2625`) |
| grid | `(1, HV, B)` | `(1, HV, B)` (`:335`) |
| arch guard | `(10, 7) → mbp = 1` | **was missing — added here** |

Both entrypoints are reachable from the public KDA decode op with `disable_state_update=True`;
`flashinfer/kda_decode.py` performs no compute-capability check.

### Why this had no coverage

Every pre-existing case in `tests/kda/test_kda_output_only.py` stays at or below **204 CTAs**
(largest is `B=17, HV=12`), a single wave on any supported part. The second trigger condition — grid
exceeds `num_sms × resident CTAs` — was therefore never met, which is why no SM107 failure had been
reported for this kernel while #4957 was filed for the GDN one.

The first commit adds that missing case (grid sized off the device SM count: `HV * B = 32` CTAs per
SM, several waves at any achievable occupancy), checked against the same fp32 recurrent reference as
its neighbours. `T` does not enter the grid, so it stays at 1 to bound the state pool.

### CI confirmation on Rubin, before the fix

Pipeline #68075462 ran the test-only commit. `unit_test_vr200_cu134` reported **32 failures** in
`tests.kda.test_kda_output_only` with
`torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`. That number is the exact signature
of the sticky fault: the new case is collection item **19 of 50**, so it is itself the first failure
and the **31** tests after it in the same process inherit the poisoned context — 32 in total. The
**18** sub-wave cases collected ahead of it all passed. B200, GB300, H100 and RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell
passed the same file on every CUDA column.

(The same job's 12 `tests.kda.test_recurrent_kda_cudnn_backend` failures are a separate, host-side
`ValueError: backend='cute-dsl' does not support this recurrent_kda prefill contract`, unrelated to
this kernel and not addressed here. The three `❔ Unknown` GB200 jobs failed before producing a JUnit
report.)

### The fix

The same exact-match `(10, 7)` guard as #5227, at both `mbp` computations. Site one reuses the `cc`
the function already queries for its cache key; site two hoists that query above the `mbp`
computation so it can do the same, rather than adding a second device query. `mbp` and `cc` are both
compile-cache-key components at both sites, so no stale module can be reused. The
`FLASHINFER_KDA_OO_MBP` override is applied after the guard and still wins, keeping the fault
reproducible on purpose.

No public API or behaviour change on any other architecture: the guard is an exact capability match,
and `mbp` does not affect results (verified bit-identical below).

## 🧪 Tests

- `tests/kda/test_kda_output_only.py::test_output_only_wy_grid_exceeds_one_wave` — new; drives
  `min_blocks_per_mp = 8` over 4736 CTAs on B200 (148 SMs) and passes in 1.5 s.
- `pytest tests/kda/test_kda_output_only.py` → **50 passed** on B200 / CUDA 13.0, unchanged by the guard.
- With the compute capability faked to `(10, 7)` on B200: `kda_wy_output_only` drops from `mbp=8` to
  `mbp=1` with **bit-identical** output (`max|d| = 0.0`) at 4736 CTAs, and `kda_recoverssm_verify`
  drops from `mbp=2` to `mbp=1` with all 8 `test_recoverssm_dropin` cases passing.
- `pre-commit run --files flashinfer/kda_kernels/kda_decode_wy_output_only.py tests/kda/test_kda_output_only.py`
  → clean.
- Rubin re-run requested below; the VR200 lane must go green on `tests/kda/` for this to merge.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Same CuTe DSL defect as #4957; sibling fix to #5227.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved compatibility on SM107 GPUs by avoiding shared-memory configuration faults in WY decode and RecoverSSM operations.
  - Added coverage for WY output-only decoding across multi-wave CTA workloads, helping validate results for larger launch configurations.

title: feat(moe): Support relu2 Accumulator (SM107)
body:
## 📌 Description

This PR adds non-gated ReLU2 support to the SM107 (Rubin) CuTe DSL fused-MoE FC1 gather/GEMM path.

This enables NVFP4 models such as NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra to use vLLM's `flashinfer_cutedsl` MoE backend on SM107. vLLM already maps `RELU2_NO_MUL` to `ActivationType.Relu2`, but FlashInfer previously rejected that activation for the Rubin kernel.

Changes include:

- Generalize the SM107 FC1 kernel from SwiGLU-only fusion to activation fusion.
- Add a non-gated epilogue that computes `relu(alpha * accumulator)^2`.
- Preserve the full GEMM1 N dimension for ReLU2 while retaining the existing halved, interleaved output layout for gated SwiGLU.
- Support optional NVFP4 output quantization and scale-factor generation on the ReLU2 path.
- Allow `ActivationType.Relu2` through SM107 dispatch and autotuning, using the activation-dependent GEMM1 dimension rather than always assuming `2 * intermediate_size`.
- Continue rejecting unsupported SM107 configurations such as GeGLU, SiTU, parameterized SwiGLU, and per-token activation scaling.

- Skip a test that explicitly forces a Blackwell-only cluster-N=2 finalize tactic; SM107 finalize tactics pin cluster-N to 1.

title: feat(sm120): instantiate 128/256-token extra-cache pages in sparse-MLA prefill
body:
## 📌 Description

`dispatch_dsv4_dual` only instantiated `extra_page_block_size == 64` (plus the 2-token WFP8 variant), so a dual-cache prefill whose candidate pool pages its extra KV cache at **128 or 256 tokens** returned `false` from the dispatcher and aborted the engine:

```
tvm.error.InternalError: Check failed: (ok) is false: Unsupported sparse-MLA prefill
configuration: model=DSV4 num_heads=8 topk=128 page_block_size=64 topk_extra=512
extra_page_block_size=128
```

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's hierarchical candidate pool is exactly that shape, so on SM120 the model could only be served by falling back to a non-FlashInfer sparse-MLA implementation.

The page size is purely an **addressing** parameter for these kernels — `prefill_kv_entry_base` derives `(idx / PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE, idx % PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE)` per token, and the only page-size-dependent special case is `USE_WFP8_ROW_XOR = DUAL_CACHE && (PAGE_BLOCK_SIZE_EXTRA == 2)`, which stays `false` for 128/256 exactly as for 64. The two sizes therefore need instantiations, not new kernel code.

This PR adds 128/256 branches to both the full-tile and the general dual-cache dispatchers (support guards + `DISPATCH_*_BY_NH_PBSX`), i.e. ten additional kernel instantiations across `num_heads ∈ {8, 16, 32, 64, 128}`.

### Performance (the reason this matters)

Serving `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on **8× RTX 6000D (SM120)**. Protocol for every row: 16k input / 512 output, concurrency 16, N=100, warmup 16 — the DeepSeek-V4 bring-up scenario.

**Like-for-like A/B, prefix caching disabled on both sides** (`--disable-radix-cache`), 3 runs each:

| prefill path | total tok/s | input tok/s | output tok/s | TTFT median | TTFT p99 | ITL median |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Triton sparse-MLA fallback (the only way to serve these shapes before this PR) | 1,978 | 1,923 | 55 | 61,539 ms | — | 64.4 ms |
| **FlashInfer with this PR** | **5,850** | 5,685 | 164 | **19,148 ms** | 35,408 ms | 26.5 ms |

* **3.0× throughput, 3.2× TTFT, 2.4× ITL** — attributable to the prefill path itself, with caching held constant.
* FlashInfer side reproduced at 5,843.69 / 5,850.38 / 5,852.39 tok/s (median 5,850.38); Triton side at 1,977.19 / 1,977.86.
* The server reaches ready with zero `Unsupported sparse-MLA prefill configuration` errors.

**In the configuration we actually serve** (prefix caching enabled, which this model's agent traffic wants), the same protocol reaches 17,950 tok/s at 963 ms median TTFT — the extra gain there is prefix reuse, not the kernel, so it is listed separately rather than folded into the number above.

## 🔍 Related Issues

No issue filed. Found while bringing DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash up on RTX 6000D (SM120); the model's candidate pool issues `extra_page_block_size` 128 and 256 at different phases of the same run, so both are added.

- [ ] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [ ] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> Not ticked: this environment has no `pre-commit`, so the hooks were not run end to end. The format-affecting hooks were run individually at the versions pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`: **clang-format 19.1.1** on `csrc/sparse_mla_sm120_prefill.cu`, and **ruff 0.12.8** (`ruff-check` + `ruff-format`) on `tests/attention/test_sparse_mla_sm120.py` — both clean. The remaining hooks (tabs, trailing whitespace, EOF) are satisfied by inspecting the diff. Please re-run `pre-commit run --all-files` on your side before merging.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

`tests/attention/test_sparse_mla_sm120.py` already parametrizes the dual-cache prefill over `extra_pbs ∈ {64, 2}` and checks numerically against `_ref_sparse_attn`. This PR extends that parametrization with `(extra_topk, extra_pbs) = (512, 128)` and `(512, 256)` across all five head counts, so the new instantiations are exercised for dispatch acceptance **and** numerical correctness. The parametrized cases fail on `main` with the dispatcher error above and pass with the patch (verified on RTX 6000D, SM120).

## Reviewer Notes

* Both dispatchers are widened for symmetry: the full-tile path (used when no `topk_length` is supplied and `topk_extra % BI == 0`) and the general dual path.
* `extra_topk` stays a runtime argument; only the page size is template-bound because it changes the KV stride, so no new launch parameters are introduced.
* If you would rather keep the instantiation set tighter, dropping `256` is safe for DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill but the model does hit it in the same end-to-end run, so both are kept.

title: cudnn prefill: return a packed LSE, declared as ragged Stats
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`cudnn_batch_prefill_with_kv_cache(..., return_lse=True)` returns the packed LSE that FlashInfer's API documents, `(total_qo_tokens, num_qo_heads)`, and declares it to cuDNN as a **ragged Stats tensor** over the query token indptr, the same packing as `q`. The historical padded `(batch, max_token_per_sequence, num_qo_heads)` buffer is still accepted when passed in explicitly.

**Why.** FlashInfer's LSE contract is a packed `[qo_len, num_qo_heads]` tensor: the wrappers allocate that shape, the cascade / merge kernels consume it, and every other backend returns it. The cuDNN low level wrote a padded per-request block instead, so a direct caller got a shape nothing downstream accepts, and the `backend="cudnn"` wrappers could not use the low level's LSE at all. #5133 fixed the ragged wrapper by computing a Stats offset on the wrapper side; this PR moves the fix into the low level, so the paged wrapper and direct callers get the packed LSE too, and the wrapper-side plumbing goes away. A ragged Stats tensor is cuDNN's sanctioned packed form: cuDNN writes each request's rows straight into the packed buffer, with no padding rows to fill with `-inf` and no gather afterwards. It is also the form the FROST engines' FlashInfer-shaped conformance suite exercises (NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1028).

**Change.** `flashinfer/cudnn/prefill.py`
- `lse=None` allocates the packed `(total_qo_tokens, h_qo)` buffer on the cuDNN graph path. The `"cubin"` backend keeps the padded form it writes.
- A passed-in `lse` may be packed or padded; any other shape is a `ValueError` naming both. It must be contiguous float32 on `q`'s device, and a passed-in `out` contiguous on `q`'s device, checked up front rather than at graph execution.
- For a packed LSE the Stats ragged offsets are derived when not given: the token-unit q indptr on the `"tokens"` path (the graph applies the `h_qo` multiplier), `batch_offsets_q // q.stride(0) * h_qo` on the element-unit path (element offsets count elements of each tensor's own storage, so a non-contiguous `q` such as a T3HD view is handled), and a device-built `[0, total]` for a single request without offsets (CUDA-graph capturable). `batch_offsets_stats` with a padded `lse` is rejected: the offsets address packed rows.
- The legacy token-to-element conversion (cuDNN too old for the direct path) uses each tensor's real token stride, as the direct path's multipliers already did.
- **NVBug 6783545 workaround (cuDNN < 9.28).** cuDNN's single-token (`s_q == 1`) GQA kernel mis-stores a ragged Stats tensor: most heads of the packed LSE are never written. Fixed in cuDNN 9.28 (MR !4496). Below that, with `max_token_per_sequence == 1` and one token per request, the padded `(b, 1, h)` block is byte-identical to the packed buffer, so the low level binds the packed buffer as the padded form (no ragged Stats offset) and returns it as packed. Ragged and paged KV. A batch that mixes zero-length and single-token requests cannot be served packed on affected versions and raises, asking for a padded `lse`.
- The graph cache key includes whether Stats carries a ragged offset. The two are different graphs; previously they shared a key.

`flashinfer/prefill.py`
- The ragged wrapper no longer computes or passes `_cudnn_stats_offsets`; the low level derives the offset from the token-unit `qo_indptr` it already receives.
- The #5245 single-token GQA guards (`auto` eligibility, explicit-cudnn `NotImplementedError` on `return_lse`) narrow to the one shape the low level cannot serve below cuDNN 9.28: a batch mixing zero-length and one-token requests. `auto` now keeps cuDNN for ordinary single-token GQA rows, LSE included.

**Behaviour change to flag:** low-level callers passing `return_lse=True, lse=None` receive the packed 2-D LSE instead of the padded 3-D one. The trace template already documented `["num_tokens", "num_heads_qo"]`. Callers that pass their own padded buffer are unchanged. vLLM and SGLang call the low level and discard the LSE.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Deferred from #4663; builds on #5133 and #5245; NVBug 6783545 (cuDNN fix MR !4496, 9.28); NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1023, #1036.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

`tests/attention/test_cudnn_prefill_lse_layout.py` (new): packed by default on both offset units × batch 1/4 × causal, checked per token against a float reference; an explicit padded buffer still works and equals the packed one request by request; non-contiguous `q` (T3HD view) on both unit paths; single-token rows, GQA and MHA, ragged and paged, with a NaN-poisoned buffer; a single request with no offsets captured into a CUDA graph; wrong shapes, wrong dtype, non-contiguous storage and padded-plus-offsets each rejected; `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper(backend="cudnn").run(return_lse=True)` returns the documented 2-D LSE matching the default backend. `test_cudnn_prefill_lse_is_base2` updated for the packed shape; the strict xfail `test_cudnn_single_token_gqa_lse_is_correct` from #5245 becomes a passing test; `test_auto_takes_cudnn_for_single_token_gqa_rows` and `test_single_token_gqa_with_empty_rows_stays_off_cudnn_lse` replace the two guard tests.

Local, 2026-09-16, cuDNN 9.27 dev (bug present) + cudnn-frontend develop (1.30), on top of main with #5133 and #5245:

| GPU | suites | result |
|---|---|---|
| H100 (sm90) | lse_layout, token_indptr, test_cudnn_prefill, deepseek, ragged_shape_override | 552 passed, 693 skipped (pre-existing shape skips) |
| H100 (sm90) | paged_cu_seqlens | 32 passed |
| B200-class (sm100) | test_auto_backend_upgrade | 36 passed |
| B200-class (sm100), `CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1`, `FLASHINFER_CUDNN_PREFILL_SHAPE_OVERRIDE=0` | lse_layout, token_indptr | 158 passed |

## Reviewer Notes

FROST engines × #5245 shape override: with `CUDNN_FRONTEND_ENABLE_FROST_ENGINES=1` and the override on, the frontend's FROST path rejects the override graph (`cu_seq_len_q must have B + 1 = 4097 elements; got 2`). This is pre-existing on main (the two `test_cudnn_wrapper_token_indptr` cases fail there the same way); this PR exposes it to the `return_lse=True` paths as well, because they now carry a Stats offset and so qualify for the override. It is a frontend-side interaction (FROST should decline override graphs and fall back), not something this PR changes; noting it here so it is tracked.

title: feat(prefill): teach the cuDNN ragged path sliding window, attention sinks and scalar scales
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Follow-up to #5133. cuDNN's SDPA supports sliding window, attention sinks and fp8 scales; the wrapper's cuDNN branch simply never handed them over, so `backend="auto"` was routing sliding-window and sink calls *past* a backend that can serve them, and a scalar scale died on a type mismatch.

**Sliding window** — mapped onto cuDNN's `diagonal_band_left_bound`. The two libraries count the band differently and the conversion was **measured, not assumed**: FlashInfer's `window_left = W` admits `W + 1` keys including the diagonal, cuDNN's `diagonal_band_left_bound = L` admits `L`. Calibrating `L` against a reference at `W-1 / W / W+1` shows `W + 1` is the match:

| cuDNN bound | vs band `[qi-(L-1), qi]` | vs `[qi-L, qi]` | vs `[qi-(L+1), qi]` |
|---|---|---|---|
| L=8 | **rel 0.0021** | 0.684 | 0.682 |
| L=32 | **rel 0.0021** | 0.354 | 0.352 |

Passing `W` through unchanged drops the oldest key of every window — an error that survives a smoke test and quietly degrades quality, so it is pinned by a test.

**Attention sinks** — bound to the SDPA `sink_token` input under a new UID. The wrapper's cuDNN branch no longer refuses when `_sinks` is set (vLLM's metadata builder stashes them there).

**Scalar scales** — `run()` advertises `q_scale: Optional[float]` and forwards it unchanged to a cuDNN call typed `Optional[torch.Tensor]`, so a float reached the variant pack and failed with `Object does not have the __dlpack__() method`. Scalars are normalised to the 1×1×1×1 fp32 tensor cuDNN expects, memoised per `(value, device)` to keep the conversion off the hot path.

`auto` eligibility splits accordingly: sliding window and sinks move out of the universal disqualifier list into a per-backend test, because cuDNN builds both into its graph while the CUTLASS run path receives only `causal` and the scales and would silently drop them. The graph cache keys on the window bound and on sink presence, so neither shares a graph with a plain causal call.

**fp8 stays off `auto` deliberately.** The scale fix means an explicit `backend="cudnn"` fp8 call now runs, but the output is not yet validated against a reference, and cuDNN's `sdpa_fp8` graph compile does not terminate for rectangular head dims — `d_qk=192, d_vo=128` was killed at >240 s at *every* size tried, down to b1/s128/h4, while every square head dim compiles in under 1 s. The stale "scale handling lives on the paths after it" rationale in the eligibility comment is corrected to say this.

The second commit fixes a CUDA-graph guard that was too strict in #5133: `fmha_varlen_plan` reallocates its work-index buffers per call, so a graph captured against plan N is stranded by plan N+1 — but planning once and *then* capturing is fine. The guard now fires only on the re-plan. This matters beyond theory: the blanket form broke `benchmarks/routines/attention.py`, which enables CUDA graphs and plans once, making every explicit-CUTLASS benchmark row fail.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Follow-up to #5133 (merged). No issue filed yet for the cuDNN `sdpa_fp8` rectangular-head-dim compile hang; happy to open one — it reproduces at the smallest constructible shape.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

**174 passed, 1 xfailed** on B200 (cc 10.0), CUDA 13.4, cuDNN 9.26.0 / frontend 1.29.0 — `tests/attention/test_auto_backend_upgrade.py` plus `tests/attention/test_cudnn_prefill_token_indptr.py`.

FA2 in this wrapper consumes neither window nor sinks (only `fmha_v2` reads `_sinks`), so there is no in-tree kernel to diff against; the new numerics tests compare against a PyTorch reference written from the definitions. All within ~0.5% relative:

| case | relative error |
|---|---|
| causal only (reference sanity) | 0.0018 |
| `window_left=16` | 0.0019 |
| `window_left=64` | 0.0018 |
| sinks | 0.0051 |
| window=32 + sinks | 0.0051 |

Plus: scalar scales accepted on the cuDNN path; CUTLASS first-plan-under-capture resolves and the re-plan routes to fa2 / raises. Four tests from #5133 asserted the old "auto declines window/sinks" policy and now encode the new one, with CUTLASS still required to stay out of both.

- The window off-by-one is the part most worth a second opinion — it is a measured mapping, and getting it wrong is silent rather than loud.
- The `auto` eligibility split is deliberate: a condition belongs in the per-backend branch when *some* backend can serve it, and in the universal list only when none can. `logits_soft_cap` and custom masks stay universal.
- Rebased onto current `main`; the `_build_prefill_graph` call collided with the new `graph_kwargs()` helper, so `window_left`/`sinks` are threaded through that helper rather than the call site, keeping the graph build and the cache-key call from drifting.

title: gemm: support partial BK128 tails in SM12x b12x MXFP8 GEMM
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

### Problem

The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 shared-expert down projection has `(M,N,K)=(6,5120,576)`. b12x rejected K not divisible by 128, excluding this shape from the native b12x path.

### Root cause

A/B TMA descriptors already use logical K and legally zero-fill the final tile. The missing protection is in scales and consumption: SF TMA stages four groups per BK128, and the last consumer executes four group-32 MMAs. Simply relaxing eligibility consumes padding scale codes. Poisoning these codes with UE8M0 NaN (255) produces NaNs in the unmodified kernel, although memcheck finds no A/B out-of-bounds access.

K=544/576/608 contain 17/18/19 groups: four full BK128 tiles followed by one/two/three live groups.

### Fix

Specialize by `K % 128` in the kernel cache. Gather only live final SF groups into small register fragments with row/group predicates, and prefetch them before full-tile computation. Skip final SF TMA/shared-memory reads, account only for A/B TMA bytes in that stage, and execute one/two/three final MMAs. Complete tiles retain TMA.

### Scope

No public A/B padding, full padded temporary, per-call workspace copy, or K=576 special case. The existing public `N,K >= 128` floor and 128x4 SF allocation layout remain. Other architecture dispatch is unchanged. Aligned K640 PTX is byte-identical to the base at M=1/6/512.

### Hardware

NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell (24 GB, SM120), disposable RunPod secure pod; driver 595.91.07, CUDA toolkit 13.0, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu130, CuTe DSL 4.7.1, cuda-python 13.0.3, Compute Sanitizer 2025.3.1.0. A separate environment also passed the focused tests on CuTe DSL 4.6.0.

title: Sm90 megamoe optimization
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Briefly describe the changes and why they’re needed. -->

### What this PR changes

1. **Kernel performance optimization** — updates the `sm90_fp8_fp8_bf16_pull_cutedsl` kernel tree and its shim/backend:
  - multi-CTA CGA execution (cluster 1x1 / 2x1 / 1x2 / 2x2, TMA multicast)
  - task-tile ping-pong scheduling across two WGMMA+epilogue warpgroups
  - two-stage FC2 R2S + TMA store pipeline
  - all six token-back x reduce mode combinations; guarded IKET ranges
  - token-bucket launch heuristics (`heuristic_config.py`): per token count the best layout / scheduling / tile / CGA / token-back config, used by default when the geometry knobs are left unset
  - shim/backend: `token_back_by_dispatch` bool -> `token_back_mode` enum, new `pingpong` / `cluster_shape_mnk` knobs
  - folded warp layout (`fold_producer_warps`, default on): with one active dispatch warp the TMA-A / TMA-B / scheduler warps move into the idle dispatch slots and the separate producer warpgroup is dropped; FC1 completion is published early from the epilogue; the freed layout makes the two-warpgroup epilogue modes pay off (blockwise 512-32768 now cooperative M64N256, +11..+45% per bucket)
  - swap-AB token tile N=8 (wgmma m64n8k32) for the per_tensor 32 / 64 / 128 buckets (+6% / +14% / +5%), with the blockwise token-scale TMA box loaded non-multicast when its per-CTA sub-box would fall below TMA's 128 B smem alignment
  - wire-level top-k dedup on dispatch and grouped combine with an optional quantized (mxfp8-style) combine wire (`dedup_dispatch` / `grouped_token_back` / `combine_format`), bit-exact with the non-dedup path at the default bf16 wire
  - 16-byte `generate_c` stores: the raw gate+up fragments are lane-transposed and written as `st.global.v4` in both layouts (non-swap 64-byte row runs, swap-AB 8x8 lane-group transpose) through a 16-byte-aligned pointer; the first version's pair stores compiled to 16-bit STGs.  generate_c overhead −5.2% → −0.9% e2e geomean (same node, 2 rounds); the generate_c=off path is unchanged
  - compact dispatch pull buffer (`compact_pull_buffer`, default on): one SMEM slot per *active* dispatch warp instead of four (misc SMEM 31264 → 9760 B per CTA), the difference goes to AB pipeline stages (per_tensor N256 cooperative 4 → 5, N128 ping-pong 7 → 8): same-node e2e +0.55% geomean (per_tensor +1.35%, pt16384 +5.4%), blockwise −0.25%
2. **Tuner + knob cache + autotune** — SM100-style tuning stack for the SM90 tree (`shim/tuner.py` / `knob_cache.py` / `autotune.py`):
  - config gains a `knobs` field: `None` resolves the persistent knob cache (`FLASHINFER_MOE_EP_KNOB_CACHE`) and falls back to the heuristic table, a dict applies explicit knobs, `"auto"` runs a collective online autotune at the first forward and persists the winner
  - autotune candidates: every geometry that wins some bucket of the heuristic table crossed with both validated token-back modes (32 candidates), derived programmatically so a table refresh updates the set
  - offline tuning CLI: `python -m flashinfer.moe_ep.tune` extended to the SM90 fp8 kernels (`--fp8-scale-mode`)
  - multirank correctness tests for `reuse_dispatch_warps` / `standalone_warps` token-back, plus host-side tuner / knob-cache / backend-wiring unit tests
3. **Benchmark alignment** — `bench_moe_ep_sm90_mega.py` adopts the block-permutation balanced routing and the low-toggle perf data recipe, heuristic launch configs and tokens 8..32768 by default, a pre-series cooldown (`--cooldown-s`), automatic CSV archiving (with the resolved heuristic config columns incl. token-back), and a `--token-back` axis; `TUNING.md` / `SKILL.md` refreshed accordingly.



### Pull backend sweep performance

**Environment.**  1 node, 4x NVIDIA H200 141GB (sm_90, SM clock locked at 1830 MHz) over NVLink, EP=4; Python 3.12, torch 2.12.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0, nvshmem4py-cu13.  All numbers in this document (the sweep below and the pull/push comparison in the next section) were taken in one session (2026-09-12) on that node, back to back, with the current heuristic table and knob defaults (`compact_pull_buffer` on).

**Method.**  `torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 benchmarks/bench_moe_ep_sm90_mega.py` (defaults): DeepSeek-V4-Pro geometry (384 experts, top-6, hidden 7168, intermediate 3072), heuristic launch config per point, block-permutation balanced routing, drop perf data recipe, 5 s cooldown before each timed series, warmup 3 + 20 barrier-aligned CUDA-event iterations.

TFLOPS = GEMM FLOPs over the max-rank time; `compute` = fused kernel + top-k reduce (zero-copy), `e2e` = full `MoEEpLayer.forward` including staging quant and output copy.
Timed-region definitions and full tables in that tree's `TUNING.md`.


| tokens/rank | per_tensor compute (tflops) | per_tensor e2e (tflops) | blockwise compute (tflops) | blockwise e2e (tflops) |
| ----------- | --------------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| 8           | 8.3                         | 7.0                     | 8.0                        | 6.2                    |

| 2048        | 549.7                       | 528.2                   | 488.7                      | 465.5                  |
| 4096        | 670.1                       | 643.1                   | 594.3                      | 554.9                  |
| 8192        | 788.5                       | 775.6                   | 735.0                      | 684.6                  |
| 16384       | 971.0                       | 916.5                   | 754.9                      | 699.5                  |
| 32768       | 941.7                       | 888.4                   | 847.7                      | 773.6                  |


Peaks: 971 TFLOPS/rank (per_tensor, 16k tokens), 848 TFLOPS/rank (blockwise, 32k tokens).

### Pull vs push comparison

- **Setup.**  Same environment and geometry as section 2; a standalone comparison harness times the full `MoEEpLayer.forward` for both backends with identical inputs (same seeds, same balanced routing) at their own DEFAULT knobs, one torchrun invocation per backend (the two communication runtimes are kept in separate processes).  All pull and push rows on this page — and the sweep table in section 2 — were taken on the **same 4x H200 node in one session, back to back** (pull per_tensor, pull blockwise, push, minutes apart, SM clock locked at 1830 MHz throughout); nodes with identical clocks and software differ by ~2% for identical configs, so never compare rows from different revisions of this page.
- **Wire precision** — pull: **FP8 E4M3 dispatch, BF16 combine**; push: **FP8 E4M3 dispatch (deduplicated), FP8 E4M3 combine** (grouped, owner-side FP32 route reduction; its grouped combine requires fp8, so combine precision is not equalized — the asymmetry favors push on combine bytes).
- **Quantization** — at defaults the two backends run DIFFERENT schemes: pull uses **per_tensor** (static calibrated fp32 scalars for activations, per-expert scalars for weights), while push is inherently **blockwise** (1x128 per-token activation blocks quantized in dispatch, 128x128 weight blocks) with no per_tensor option.
per_tensor dequantization is cheaper in the GEMMs, so the default comparison favors pull on compute; a scale-mode-equalized comparison (pull run with `fp8_scale_mode="blockwise"`) is included below.
- **Timing recipe**: barrier-aligned CUDA events, 20 warmups + 100 samples, p50 per rank, max across ranks; 5 s cooldown per point.


| tokens/rank | pull p50 (ms) | push p50 (ms) | pull/push speedup |
| ----------- | ------------- | ------------- | ----------------- |
| 8           | 0.853         | 0.859         | 1.01x             |
| 16          | 1.322         | 1.408         | 1.07x             |
| 32          | 1.444         | 1.700         | 1.18x             |
| 64          | 1.769         | 1.911         | 1.08x             |
| 128         | 1.829         | 2.005         | 1.10x             |
| 256         | 1.705         | 2.026         | 1.19x             |
| 512         | 1.765         | 2.139         | 1.21x             |
| 1024        | 2.215         | 2.318         | 1.05x             |
| 2048        | 3.039         | 3.295         | 1.08x             |
| 4096        | 5.033         | 5.472         | 1.09x             |
| 8192        | 8.559         | 10.149        | 1.19x             |
| 16384       | 14.636        | 20.485        | 1.40x             |
| 32768       | 30.483        | 41.465        | 1.36x             |


Pull is faster at all 13 points: 1.01-1.21x at 8-512 tokens (1.01x at 8 tokens, 1.07-1.21x from 16 tokens up), 1.05-1.09x at 1k-4k tokens, and 1.19-1.40x from 8k tokens up (the compact pull buffer's extra AB stage lifts the 16k / 32k per_tensor points to 1.40x / 1.36x).

**Scale-mode-equalized comparison (both blockwise).**  Same protocol, pull run with `fp8_scale_mode="blockwise"` so both sides pay the same 1x128/128x128 dequantization cost:


| tokens/rank | pull-blockwise p50 (ms) | push p50 (ms) | pull/push speedup |
| ----------- | ----------------------- | ------------- | ----------------- |
| 8           | 0.946                   | 0.859         | 0.91x             |
| 16          | 1.286                   | 1.408         | 1.09x             |
| 32          | 1.807                   | 1.700         | 0.94x             |
| 64          | 1.722                   | 1.911         | 1.11x             |
| 128         | 1.749                   | 2.005         | 1.15x             |
| 256         | 2.221                   | 2.026         | 0.91x             |
| 512         | 1.870                   | 2.139         | 1.14x             |
| 1024        | 2.454                   | 2.318         | 0.94x             |
| 2048        | 3.487                   | 3.295         | 0.94x             |
| 4096        | 5.860                   | 5.472         | 0.93x             |
| 8192        | 9.673                   | 10.149        | 1.05x             |
| 16384       | 20.014                  | 20.485        | 1.02x             |
| 32768       | 35.139                  | 41.465        | 1.18x             |


Under equal blockwise quantization pull leads at 16, 64, 128, 512, 8192, 16384, 32768 tokens (1.02-1.18x) and push leads at 8, 32, 256, 1024, 2048, 4096 tokens (pull at 0.91-0.94x).
The default-vs-default result above therefore rests on pull's per_tensor mode; per_tensor requires offline-calibrated activation scales identical on every rank, whereas blockwise needs no calibration — the two modes also differ in accuracy/deployment requirements, not just speed.

title: prims_ts: add c_row_stride to decouple C pitch from output width
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

The swapAB C layout used `output_m_for_c` as both extent and stride, so the output
buffer had to be exactly as wide as the launch's own output. This threads
`c_row_stride` from `gemm()` down to `GmemCResource` and uses it for the stride only;
extent and bounds checks still use `output_m_for_c`.

Defaults to the launch's own width, so existing callers are unchanged.
`build_fp8_per_tensor_launch_io()` accepts it and validates alignment, stride and
storage bounds.

Needed for a MoE expert-weight split, where FC1/FC2 partitions do strided fills into
one shared output. That consumer follows separately — the tests below are what make
this verifiable on its own rather than an unused parameter.

**Scope, deliberately narrow:**

- **swapAB only.** Non-swapAB still hardcodes its pitch to `n`; the two store sites in
  `_store_non_swap_32x32b` and the `c_layout` stride are the extension point.
- **Not valid with block-scaled output.** `_sf_c_index` and `_dsfp8_c_scale_idx` still
  derive from the launch's own output width, so a shared buffer would get wrong scale
  factors. Unreachable today — this path is per-tensor FP8 with no SFs — but unenforced
  in the kernel.

New `tests/prims_ts/test_batched_gemm_c_row_stride.py` — 15 cases, all bit-exact
(`max_abs=0.000000` against the PyTorch reference):

- direct `gC.store` **and** TMA descriptor store paths
- BF16 output, and gated FP8 output (half-width)
- pitch == width, and wider (96 / 128 / 160 / 256)

`reference_check` gains `c_row_stride` / `c_partition_offset` so a launch can write into
a wider shared buffer. The slack is sentinel-filled and asserted untouched after the
launch — that assertion is what distinguishes a correct pitch from the default, since

title: feat(attention): bound batch prefill/decode workspace over a shape range
body:
## 📌 Description

`workspace_size()` reports the memory needed by one concrete `plan()`. Some callers have to reserve memory earlier, when they only know the scheduler limits, so probing a few representative shapes is not enough.

This PR adds `workspace_size_upper_bound()` to batch prefill and batch decode. It takes the largest batch, query-row and paged-KV limits and returns conservative float and integer workspace sizes for plans within those limits. The calculation follows the scheduler's tile and split rules and uses the same allocation order as planning.

Existing planning and execution are unchanged. Callers opt in by using the new method. If the selected backend cannot provide a bound, the method raises `NotImplementedError` so the caller can keep its existing allocation.

Focused validation:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/attention/test_workspace_size_upper_bound.py -q
python -m py_compile flashinfer/prefill.py flashinfer/decode.py
ruff check flashinfer/prefill.py flashinfer/decode.py tests/attention/test_workspace_size_upper_bound.py
ruff format --check flashinfer/prefill.py flashinfer/decode.py
clang-format --dry-run --Werror csrc/batch_prefill.cu csrc/batch_prefill_jit_binding.cu csrc/batch_decode.cu csrc/batch_decode_jit_binding.cu include/flashinfer/attention/scheduler.cuh include/flashinfer/utils.cuh
```

`14` CPU cases and `21` GPU cases passed, for `35 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped` on one SM80 device. The first JIT build took about four minutes in this environment; the test run completed in `0.65s` with the module already built.

The GPU cases compare the bound with the real planner over targeted non-uniform request shapes, tile-boundary query lengths, the default and fixed split paths, split disabled, both decode planners, and eager and CUDA graph planner modes. They are targeted checks rather than an exhaustive enumeration. The CUDA graph cases exercise planner sizing in graph mode; they do not capture or replay a graph.

Not run: serving or measurement of the memory recovered by a caller using the bound.

## Reviewer Notes

The C++ bound in `scheduler.cuh` is the part I would most like reviewed, especially the default split, fixed split and CUDA graph mode branches.

The Python changes keep backend resolution shared between `plan()`, `workspace_size()` and the new upper-bound method, then expose the entry points through the existing module facades. FA3, cuDNN and TRTLLM paths without an upper-bound entry point remain unsupported and raise `NotImplementedError`.

title: test(attention): exercise the NVFP4 split-KV gated path on hardware
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`_nvfp4_kv_requires_disabled_split_kv` disables split-KV for NVFP4 KV as an empirical
workaround whose root cause is, by its own docstring, unconfirmed. #4747 scoped it to
`_NVFP4_SPLIT_KV_BROKEN_ARCHS = ((12, 0), (12, 1))`, so SM120/121 are now the only architectures
carrying it.

Nothing currently runs the configuration the gate disables. The two tests that cover it,
`test_nvfp4_split_kv_gate_dtype_logic` and `test_nvfp4_split_kv_gate_arch_scope`, are a dtype
classification check and an architecture-scoping check with a faked compute capability; both run
without a GPU, and `disable_split_kv` does not appear in that file. So on the parts that pay for the
workaround its premise is untestable today: the gate could stop being a no-op, or stop being
necessary, and CI would not notice either way.

This adds one test to `tests/attention/test_batch_prefill_kernels.py`, next to the NVFP4 paged
prefill tests whose helpers it reuses, plus `_PLAN_INFO_SPLIT_KV_IDX` alongside the existing
`_PLAN_INFO_CTA_TILE_Q_IDX`. It runs the same inputs twice through the FA2 NVFP4 paged prefill entry
point -- once with split-KV force-disabled as the gate does today, once with the gate bypassed via
`monkeypatch` exactly as `test_nvfp4_split_kv_gate_arch_scope` already does -- and pins:

- the gated run does not select split-KV and the bypassed run does, both read from `PrefillPlanInfo`
  rather than assumed;
- both runs are within the tolerance the neighbouring NVFP4 tests use of a float32 dequantization
  oracle built with `nvfp4_to_float` from the exact quantized bytes the kernel reads, so it is a
  dequantization reference and not a requantized approximation;
- allowing split-KV does not move the result more than 2x further from that oracle than the gated
  run already is. Split-KV changes the softmax reduction order, so some drift is expected; the
  largest split/non-split ratio reported on an affected part in #4749 is about 1.4x, so 2x leaves
  room for reduction-order drift without admitting the corruption the gate exists for.

Parametrized over symmetric `head_dim` 128 and the asymmetric (512, 256) shape the gate was added
alongside in 8f9ad200, at `qo_len` 1 and 16 against long KV, which is the `qo_len << kv_len` regime
the docstring names. It self-skips where the gate is not in force, so it is a no-op on every
architecture #4747 exempted.

The gate is not left unexercised for lack of hardware in CI: the internal matrix already has
`unit_test_rtx_pro_6000` and `unit_test_5090` at cc 12.0 and `unit_test_spark` at cc 12.1.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- #4749 -- the open issue tracking the unconfirmed root cause. This PR does not change the gate;
  whether the workaround should be narrowed further or removed belongs there.

title: feat(prefill): `lse_base` and `lse_layout` on the prefill wrappers (defaults unchanged; "ln" / "HN" for LSE-merge consumers)
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

`BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper.run()` and `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper.run()` (and the `cudnn_batch_prefill_with_kv_cache` entry point) take two new keywords. **`lse_base`**:

- `"log2"` (default): exactly what the wrappers return today, bit-for-bit. FlashInfer's kernels fold `log2(e)` into the softmax scale and emit `max + log2(sum(exp2(...)))`.
- `"ln"`: the natural-log LSE, `torch.logsumexp` of the scaled scores, which is what LSE merges written with `expf` consume (vLLM's `merge_attn_states`, its DCP all-gather/all-to-all reductions, FA's own convention).

Why: an LSE consumer has to know the base, and today the only way to get natural log out of FlashInfer is to multiply afterwards. The cuDNN backend actually *produces* natural-log stats and converts them to base 2 with a Python-side `mul_`; vLLM's DCP prefill then converts them back (`log2_lse_to_ln`) before merging. Two elementwise kernels and two host-side dispatches per layer per step, for a number that was already in the requested form when it left the kernel. With `lse_base="ln"` the cuDNN path hands out its stats as written; every other backend applies one `ln 2` rescale, the same cost a caller pays today, so the caller can drop its own conversion for all backends at once.

**`lse_layout`**: `"NH"` (default) is today's `[qo_indptr[-1], num_qo_heads]`; `"HN"` returns the contiguous transpose `[num_qo_heads, qo_indptr[-1]]`, the layout LSE merge kernels take (vLLM's `merge_attn_states`, FlashInfer's own `merge_state` variants). The kernels still write `[tokens, heads]`; `"HN"` is finished by one fused kernel (`copy_` or `torch.mul(..., out=)` of the transposed view, 5-6 µs host), into a caller-provided `[heads, tokens]` buffer when given. Today's caller does `lse.transpose(0, 1).contiguous() * ln2`, two kernels and ~12 µs host, per LSE. When the cuDNN graph can carry the LSE strides at execute time (#5245's override path) the cuDNN backend will write `"HN"` directly with zero extra kernels; that wiring is a follow-up.

Semantics are the wrapper's, not the backend's: a caller asking for `"ln"` gets `"ln"` from fa2, fa3, cutlass, cuDNN, cute-dsl, cute-dsl-prims and cutile alike (base-2 kernels are rescaled in place; the cuDNN cubin fallback raises `NotImplementedError` for `"ln"`). Invalid values raise `ValueError` before any kernel runs. The `lse=` output buffer is honored in the requested base.

Host cost per `run(return_lse=True)`, ragged wrapper, b=64 rows × q_len 4, kv 1024, GQA 8/2, d=128 bf16, SM100 board (148 SMs), cuDNN 9.27 / cudnn-frontend 1.30, medians of 2000 (run-to-run noise ≈ ±5 µs):

| backend | `"log2"`, `"NH"` (default, today) | `"ln"`, `"NH"` | `"log2"`, `"HN"` | `"ln"`, `"HN"` | today's caller glue on top of the default (`transpose.contiguous() * ln2`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cuDNN | 61.1 µs | 45.1 µs | 80.2 µs | 68.0 µs | +12.4 µs |
| fa2 | 20.1 µs | 27.4 µs | 32.0 µs | 34.4 µs | +12.5 µs |

`"ln"` on cuDNN removes the `log2e` multiply (and its launch); on fa2 it adds the `ln 2` multiply the caller runs today. `"HN"` costs one transpose kernel in either base (fused with the rescale for `"ln"`), i.e. the caller's two kernels become one inside FlashInfer, and become zero for cuDNN once the graph writes the layout itself.

For vLLM's FlashInfer DCP prefill this means: pass `lse_base="ln", lse_layout="HN"` to both `run(..., return_lse=True)` calls, delete the two `log2_lse_to_ln(lse.transpose(0, 1).contiguous())` lines, and set `is_lse_base_on_e=True` on the DCP combine: the merge consumes the kernels' LSE with no conversion or copy on the caller's side.

Follow-ups, not in this PR:
- fa2/fa3 can emit natural log directly (the store site is `m + log2(d)`; a scale on the write) so `"ln"` costs nothing there either.
- cuDNN writing `"HN"` directly through the Stats strides (needs execute-time strides, i.e. on top of #5245).
- With cudnn-frontend's `stats_use_log2` (NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#931, cuDNN 9.28) the cuDNN `"log2"` path also loses its multiply; this PR is where that flag will be wired.

The new test pins it as a strict xfail.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Companion to #5245 (cuDNN ragged graph reuse + single-token GQA guard); the natural-log conversion it inherits is the one `"ln"` removes. Frontend/backend side of the same convention problem: NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#931, cudnn/cudnn!4402 (internal). Context: #4663 (the double conversion that motivated owning the base at the API).

- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

New `tests/attention/test_lse_base.py`, ragged and paged wrappers, causal and non-causal, GQA 8/2 d=128 bf16 with three variable-length requests: the default is `torch.equal` to `lse_base="log2"`; `"ln"` matches a float32 `torch.logsumexp` reference (bottom-right causal) and equals the base-2 result × `ln 2`; the output tensor is unchanged; `"HN"` in both bases is contiguous `[heads, tokens]` and bit-equal to the `"NH"` transpose; caller-provided `lse` buffers are filled in the requested base and layout, a wrong-shape buffer raises; `lse_base="e"` / `lse_layout="TH"` raise. Backends are chosen per machine: fa2 everywhere, fa3 on SM90a, cutlass + cute-dsl (FMHA route at d=128, modular kernel at d=64) + cuDNN (when the frontend is importable) on SM100a; paged cuDNN strict-xfailed, see above.

- SM100 (148 SMs), cuDNN 9.27 / cudnn-frontend 1.30: 14 passed, 2 xfailed.
- H100: 8 passed, 2 skipped (the cute-dsl modular case is SM100a-only).

## Reviewer Notes

- Default behaviour is untouched by construction: `_finish_lse` is a no-op for (`"log2"`, `"NH"`), and the cuDNN multiply is still applied for `"log2"`. The `torch.equal(default, "log2")` assertions cover every backend the machine has.
- Every early return that hands the caller's `lse` to a kernel (paged cute-dsl-prims, paged cute-dsl, ragged cute-dsl FMHA / modular) first goes through `_stage_lse`, so the kernel always writes `[tokens, heads]` and the caller's `"HN"` buffer is only ever the finisher's destination (must be contiguous).
- The cuDNN branch of each wrapper passes `lse_base` down and skips the wrapper-level rescale; all other branches rescale at their return. The paged wrapper has one common tail, guarded on `self._backend != "cudnn"`.

title: fix(gemm): fall back from stale MXFP8 split-K tactics
body:
## Description

Fix a serving startup failure in the CuTe DSL MXFP8 GEMM runner when an
autotuned low-M split-K tactic is reused for a runtime shape outside the
split-K kernel's validity range.

The autotuner deliberately buckets dynamic M dimensions. A cached tactic can
therefore be a valid optimization for the bucket's profiling shape while being
invalid for the concrete runtime shape. `CuteDSLMxfp8GemmRunner` previously
turned that stale optimization into a hard failure:

```text
ValueError: Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic: ((128, 32), (1, 1), True, False, 2)
```

This change preserves strict validation for structurally malformed split-K
tactics, but falls back to the runner's existing non-split-K tactic when only
the runtime shape or output layout is incompatible. This matches
`TunableRunner`'s fallback contract and keeps a stale optimization from taking
down model serving.

A regression test passes a tactic valid for M=32 to an M=64 invocation and
checks the fallback result against `torch.mm`.

## Related Issues

N/A

## Tests

- `python3 -m compileall -q flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py tests/gemm/test_mm_mxfp8.py`
- `git diff --check`
- End-to-end reproduction on 4x GB300 with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4,
  `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, FlashInfer autotuning enabled, and
  `FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel` enabled:
  - all four ranks completed the 4096-token / 20-bucket autotune;
  - the previous `Invalid MXFP8 split-K tactic` exception did not recur;
  - the vLLM endpoint became healthy;
  - 8/8 smoke requests succeeded.

runner logic is still present on current `main`; the PR and regression test are
based on current upstream `main`.
